description: Find a data center site in the US by MW, state and energization date. Invariant lists powered sites from 1 MW to 1.5 GW and shows how to verify the power behind each one.
intro: Invariant finds data center sites for buyers across the US, from energized 1 MW edge and mining sites to a 1.5 GW AI campus. The method is the same at every size: start from power evidence, rule out sites that cannot close, then match land. This page sets out what each size needs, how to grade a site’s power, the 2026 rules that change the search, and the sites we have now. Tell us your MW, states and date, and we send the ones that fit.
takeaways: Search from power first. Land is rarely the constraint; deliverable MW on a date is.
Grade each site by the document behind its MW: map, proximity, named MW, utility study, signed agreement.
Size changes everything: 1 to 10 MW sits on distribution, 20 to 100 MW needs a substation, 200 MW and up is a transmission project.
Invariant lists US sites from 1 MW to 1.5 GW and finds off-market ones on request.

sections.heading: Start from power, not land

blocks.text: Most data center site searches start with a parcel and a line on a map. That is backwards. Land is plentiful almost everywhere in the US. Deliverable power on a known date is not. In a 2025 analysis of ERCOT, Paces found only about 17% of substations near suitable land had any withdrawal headroom. The rest of the land was stranded.

So the search runs in this order. Pick the MW and the date. Find stations, plants and energized loads that can carry it. Kill anything claimed, contaminated or under a moratorium. Then look at parcels around what survives. Finally, grade each site by the document behind its MW.

sections.heading: Grid rules that change the search in 2026

blocks.text: In Texas, SB 6 rules apply to new ERCOT loads of 75 MW and up, and since August 3, 2026 ERCOT has not approved energization of new data centers of that size while Batch Zero studies run. TCEQ has also paused data center permits statewide.

Elsewhere, utilities are adding large-load tariffs with study fees, collateral, minimum bills near 80 to 85% of contract demand and terms of 12 to 15 years. AEP Ohio’s data center tariff is an early public example. PJM’s long-term forecast keeps rising on data center demand.
Local approval is the other filter. Data Center Watch tracks projects blocked or delayed by local opposition, and counties from Missouri to Arizona have passed temporary bans or new rules.

description: Find a 1 MW data center site in the US: energized edge, inference and mining sites, what 1 MW really fits, the service you need and how fast it can be live.
intro: A 1 MW data center site is the easiest size to find and the easiest to get wrong. At this scale you are almost always on the utility distribution system, so the fastest sites are buildings or yards that already have the service in place. A new 1 MW service can take longer than people expect because of transformer lead times and feeder upgrades. Invariant keeps a running list of energized small sites across the US, from 0.5 MW turnkey mining yards to Tier III rooms, and shares the ones that fit on a call.
takeaways: 1 MW at the meter is about 0.75 MW of IT at a PUE of 1.3. That is roughly six 120 kW AI racks, or a few hundred air-cooled mining machines.
At this size the question is the existing service: voltage, transformer rating and whether the feeder has room. A site that already has it can be live in weeks.
Land is rarely the issue. A containerized 1 MW deployment fits on well under an acre.
Ask for a recent utility bill or a service letter showing the transformer and the contracted capacity, not a map of nearby lines.

sections.heading: What 1 MW actually fits

blocks.text: Utilities sell facility load. Tenants buy IT load. At a PUE of 1.3, a 1 MW site leaves about 0.8 MW for IT. At about 120 kW per NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 rack, that is roughly 6.4 racks, or about 460 GPUs. Air-cooled designs at 30 to 50 kW per rack fit more racks and fewer GPUs per MW. Typical buyers at this size are edge inference, a small GPU pod, enterprise compute or a bitcoin mining deployment.

rows: Utility distribution service. Usually a pad-mounted transformer stepping a 12 to 35 kV feeder down to 480 V, sometimes primary service at the feeder voltage.
Under 1 acre for containers; a small warehouse or retrofit room for a built facility.

sections.heading: Where 1 MW sites come from

blocks.text: Most 1 MW sites we see are one of four things: a light industrial building with a large existing service, a small mining yard with containers already wired, a room inside a colocation facility, or a spot inside the fence of a power plant or industrial user that has spare capacity on its own transformers.

Each has a different catch. Industrial buildings often have the amps but not the cooling. Mining yards have power and airflow but no redundancy. Colocation rooms are fast and expensive per kW. Plant sites can be the cheapest power you will ever see, with the least flexibility on hours and terms.

blocks.text: Confirm the contracted capacity on the bill, not the panel rating. A building with a 4,000 A switchboard at 480 V can in theory carry more than 3 MW, yet its utility contract and transformer may cap it far lower.
Ask whether the power is firm or interruptible. Many small mining sites run on curtailable rates. That suits miners and does not suit an inference customer with an uptime promise.

title: 5 MW data center site: finding energized power for a 5 MW load in the US
description: Find a 5 MW data center site in the US: turnkey energized sites, how many racks 5 MW fits, the feeder and transformer you need and how long new service takes.
intro: 5 MW is where a data center site stops being a building with a big service and starts needing its own utility plan. A 5 MW load is usually still on a distribution feeder, often a dedicated one, and that feeder decides the timeline. Turnkey 5 MW sites with transformers already energized come up regularly in mining markets, and they convert well to inference and edge use if the power is firm. Invariant tracks several of them across the US right now.
takeaways: 5 MW at the meter is about 3.8 MW of IT at a PUE of 1.3, roughly 32 AI racks at 120 kW, or 2,300 GPUs.
Expect medium-voltage distribution service, often a dedicated 12 to 35 kV feeder and several pad-mounted transformers.
Turnkey mining sites at 5 MW can be live immediately. Check whether the rate is interruptible before you plan an uptime promise around it.
Land: 1 to 5 acres covers most layouts, more if you add generators and cooling yards.

blocks.text: Utilities sell facility load. Tenants buy IT load. At a PUE of 1.3, a 5 MW site leaves about 3.8 MW for IT. At about 120 kW per NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 rack, that is roughly 32 racks, or about 2,310 GPUs. Air-cooled designs at 30 to 50 kW per rack fit more racks and fewer GPUs per MW. Typical buyers at this size are an inference cluster, a regional colocation room, an enterprise build or a mining expansion.

rows: Medium-voltage distribution, typically 12.47 to 34.5 kV, often a dedicated feeder or a large share of one, with several transformers on site.
About 1 to 5 acres depending on containers versus a built hall and whether backup generation sits on site.
Immediate for energized turnkey sites. New service commonly runs 9 to 24 months where a feeder extension or substation bay is needed.
Contract demand on the bill, the utility one-line diagram, transformer ratings, a written statement of feeder headroom, and the rate schedule (firm or curtailable).

sections.heading: Why 5 MW sites move fast or not at all

blocks.text: A single 12.47 kV distribution feeder carries roughly 8 to 12 MW in normal operation, and utilities rarely give one customer most of it. So a new 5 MW load often means a dedicated feeder from the substation, a new breaker position or a new circuit, and each of those has its own queue and equipment lead time.
That is why energized 5 MW sites trade at a premium. The value is in the transformers and the feeder that are already there, with the utility already billing the account.

sections.heading: Converting a 5 MW mining site to AI or inference

blocks.text: Mining sites at this size have the power and usually the airflow. What they lack is redundancy, backup generation and a building that meets an enterprise tenant’s checklist. Budget for UPS, generators, fire protection and either liquid cooling or a new hall. Keep the utility service and the land; plan to rebuild most of the rest. title: 10 MW Data Center Sites for Sale or Lease
description: Compare published 10 MW data center and powered-site leads. Check which MW figure is at the meter, what reaches the racks, and what a buyer can secure.
intro: Start with the kind of 10 MW you need. An AI or colocation tenant usually needs a committed block of critical IT power in a fitted hall. A developer looking for powered land needs a utility service commitment at the meter. Under an illustrative 1.30 facility-to-IT design ratio, 10 MW of facility power supports about 7.7 MW of IT load. This guide shows what four published offers say and what is still needed to make each one actionable.
takeaways: For a 10 MW IT deployment, ask the operator to quote contiguous, unallocated critical IT capacity and a handover date for the specific hall.
For powered land, ask for the serving utility, the meter or point of delivery, the service agreement, and written confirmation of what can transfer.
The examples below include a broker listing with a past delivery date, a planned new build, and two published Invariant leads. Current allocations require a fresh quote.

sections.heading: Where to look for a 10 MW site

blocks.text: The 10 MW figure means something different in each of these records. The table uses the broker or operator’s own description, then identifies the missing fact that controls whether a buyer can proceed. Public materials reviewed November 22, 2026.

One facility is marketed as 4 MW built, with a second phase to reach 10 MW of critical IT. The portfolio includes separate, smaller offers.
Ask what is contractable in the 4 MW phase and what fit-out, cooling work and commissioning are needed to reach 10 MW.

blocks.text: For a near-term move, call the broker or operator first and ask for a dated availability sheet. For a longer runway, ask the developer for remaining milestones and the documents that control delivery. The two lists will look different even when the headline MW is identical.

sections.heading: How much IT load fits in a 10 MW data center?

blocks.text: Facility demand includes the IT equipment and the systems that keep it running, such as cooling and power conversion. Critical IT capacity is the portion specified for the IT equipment. The table uses an illustrative ratio of 1.30 between concurrent facility and IT demand for early sizing. Power usage effectiveness, or PUE, is commonly reported as an annual energy ratio. Ask the engineer to calculate peak facility demand for the contracted operating conditions.

columns: What the buyer should ask for
rows: Peak summer cooling and electrical limits, with design margin.
The utility demand underpinning the offer and the operator’s guaranteed IT allocation.

blocks.text: NVIDIA’s GB200 NVL72 example uses about 120 kW at full load for a rack with 72 GPUs. On a 10 MW facility supply, the 7.69 MW illustrative IT budget gives a mathematical ceiling of 64 racks, or 4,608 GPUs. Reserve 0.60 MW of that IT budget for external network and storage equipment and spare capacity, and the example drops to 59 racks, or 4,248 GPUs. The final count depends on how much power and cooling each rack position can support.

sections.heading: What to ask for before a site tour

items: Power allocation. Ask for a written offer specifying MW, measurement point, committed capacity, handover date, and the allowable ramp.

Electrical and cooling capacity. Request a one-line diagram, meaning the drawing of the electrical path from utility to rack. Confirm rack density, cooling method, and what stays available during maintenance or a component failure.
Network and commissioning. Check carrier routes and entry points. Ask what acceptance tests are complete and which upgrades remain.
Commercial rights. Identify who can sign, what consent a lease or sale requires, and when the power allocation expires.

sections.heading: Built facility, energized conversion, or powered land?

blocks.text: Start with a fitted hall when the IT handover date drives the deal. An energized industrial or mining site may shorten the work at the meter, but a conversion still needs to prove cooling, backup power, fiber, and permitted use. Greenfield gives the most control over design. Build the schedule from the utility’s scope and milestones, then add construction and commissioning.

title: AI data center site: finding power and land for a GPU cluster in the US (2026)
description: Find a site for an AI data center or GPU cluster in the US: power density, liquid cooling, MW per GPU, firm power and the AI-ready sites Invariant has available now.
intro: An AI data center site has to deliver more power to less floor space than any facility before it. A single NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 rack draws about 120 kW and needs liquid cooling. What changes for site selection is the power: AI tenants need firm service, a fast ramp and room to grow, often from tens of MW to hundreds. Invariant matches AI buyers to sites with documented power, from energized 10 MW inference sites to a 1.5 GW campus.
takeaways: A GB200 NVL72 rack draws about 120 kW. 1,000 GPUs need roughly 2 MW at the meter including cooling.
AI tenants need firm power. Curtailable mining rates do not work for most AI contracts.
Plan for liquid cooling and heat rejection outdoors; land per MW falls less than rack density suggests.
Invariant lists AI-ready sites from 10 MW inference to 1.5 GW training campuses.

sections.heading: Power per GPU

blocks.text: At about 120 kW per 72-GPU rack, each GPU draws roughly 1.7 kW at the rack. Add cooling and power losses at a PUE of 1.3 and 1,000 GPUs need about 2.2 MW at the meter. A 100,000 GPU cluster needs over 200 MW. Training and inference differ: inference fits in 5 to 50 MW sites near users, training wants hundreds of MW in one place.

sections.heading: Firm power and redundancy

blocks.text: Many energized sites on the market were built for bitcoin mining on interruptible rates. AI tenants usually need firm service with backup. Read the power contract before pricing a conversion, and budget for generators, UPS and a second feed where the tenant requires them.

sections.heading: Cooling and land

blocks.text: Liquid cooling shrinks the building per MW but still rejects heat outside through dry coolers or towers. Substations and cooling yards scale with MW, so an AI campus still needs roughly 0.7 to 2 MW per gross acre.

faqs.answer: Invariant compares U.S. candidate sites against your facility load, service dates, location and site requirements. The shortlist shows the evidence behind the power claims and the open items to resolve before you advance a candidate.

faqs.question: Can Invariant review a data center site I already have?
faqs.answer: Yes. Provide the parcel or coordinates, load by phase and any documents behind the marketed power. The work can include a feasibility screen or independent power-flow analysis, depending on the decision you need to make.

faqs.question: What do I need to request a site search?
faqs.answer: Share target markets, facility MW at the meter by phase, required service dates and whether you want to buy, lease or develop. Add any reliability, cooling or fiber requirements that could rule out a site.
